title: Adaptive Authority Runtime and Audit Proxy for RBAC v2
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Build a compact, high-throughput policy evaluation runtime and a sidecar-like audit proxy to enforce RBAC v2 across API, runtime, and console surfaces. Goals: 1) deterministic, low-latency authorization checks for per-request policy decisions; 2) rich, tamper-evident audit events emitted for every decision; 3) easy integration points for SSO/SAML identity assertions and admin controls; 4) seamless rollouts with canarying and automatic fallback to safe defaults. This ticket covers the runtime evaluator, a lightweight authorization middleware (gRPC/HTTP) used by runtime and API, the audit enrichment service, and console integration hooks for admin-level controls.

Scope:
- Implement a compact policy evaluator that supports the RBAC v2 rule model, attribute-based conditions, and versioned policy bundles.
- Provide a pluggable adapter layer so console/API/runtime can call the same evaluation surface (HTTP/gRPC).
- Implement evaluation caching (per-request token KV + short-lived result cache) with invalidation tied to policy bundle updates.
- Build Audit Proxy that records decision context (actor, principal attributes, request path, model, route, cache_hit, decision_reason) and streams events to our audit pipeline (Kafka). Events must be signed/hmaced for integrity before leaving the host.
- Add SSO/SAML hooks: normalize identity claims from IdP into a canonical principal structure consumed by evaluator.
- Admin controls: expose runtime flags (allowlist overrides, emergency breakglass) that can be toggled from Console and surface in audit logs.
- Observability: per-eval latency histograms, cache hit ratio, bundle load times, and error traces.

Out of scope for this ticket: long-term policy authoring UI, migration of existing RBAC policies (will be a follow-up), and cross-region audit archival retention policy (ops work).
acceptance_criteria: Authorization middleware implements gRPC + HTTP endpoints and responds with allow/deny/conditional decisions in <5ms median under synthetic load
Policy bundles can be uploaded and versioned; evaluation uses the pinned bundle version for a tenancy
Audit Proxy emits signed JSON events to Kafka topic 'audit.decisions' and events include canonical principal, request metadata, cache_hit, and policy_version
SAML/SSO adapter normalizes at least two IdP claim formats (Okta, OneLogin) in staging and produces a canonical principal for evaluation
Admin breakglass toggle is callable from Console REST and is evaluated with higher precedence than normal rules
Canary rollout path: 10% of requests routed to new evaluator for 48 hours with auto-rollback on error rate >0.5% or p99 eval latency increase >2x
Unit and integration tests cover evaluator logic, cache invalidation, audit signing, and SSO normalization paths
Documentation: design doc and runbook published, and a migration checklist for existing policies added to docs link
technical_notes: Policy language: choose a simplified JSON-based rule format (fast parse) with an optional Rego translation layer for complex policies; keep evaluator implementation native to reduce overhead
Evaluation architecture: single-file in-memory index per tenant loaded by versioned bundle, deterministic rule ordering to avoid flakiness
Cache strategy: LRU per-process cache keyed by (principal_hash, resource, action, policy_version), TTL 30s, explicit invalidation on bundle update
Audit integrity: events HMAC-signed using node-local key rotated weekly and published hash to audit-metadata topic for verification
SSO normalization: implement an adapter interface with schema mapping rules; perform attribute mapping in middleware before calling evaluator
Admin controls: persisted in config service with change events broadcast over the same bundle bus to ensure consistent enforcement
Failure modes: on evaluator crash or timeout, default to deny for console admin APIs and fail-open for non-admin read-only inference requests with an auditable 'fail_open' flag
Performance target: median eval latency <5ms, p99 <15ms under 5000 RPS per-node synthetic workload
Security review: include threat model for audit tampering, bundle poisoning, and SSO claim spoofing
